DNA double strand breakage by a Ca/Mg-dependent human endonuclease is more efficient than by other endonucleases in the initiation of DNA recombination.
Ca/Mg-dependent DNA endonuclease is involved in the initiation of DNA recombination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of DNA recombination by the Ca/Mg-dependent nuclear endonuclease.
the development of a new approach to the study of the mechanisms and regulation of recombination.
the development of the system for the study of recombination in vitro and with the analysis of DNA recombination initiated by endonucleases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca/Mg endonuclease is an endonuclease that cuts DNA in a calcium and magnesium dependent manner.
the Ca/Mg-dependent enzyme is not a recombinase, but it may be a part of a recombinase complex.
Ca/Mg-dependent DNA endonuclease is a very important and essential enzyme in DNA recombination in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca/Mg-dependent enzyme of the lymphocytes nuclei is a new type of the recombinogenic enzyme.
